Split into nine children: two new reusable lemmas (tau_current, triple_inter_open) and seven comparator-accepted declarations reused by name with byte-identical frozen types (no new DAG node for those). WHY THIS SPLIT. The supplied proof combines three kinds of ingredients.
(i) Facts about τ-currents of rectifiable triples, which are new obligations:
 - (H0)/(H2): "the τ-integral of a triple is linear and sequentially continuous, i.e. a current". This is tau_current = br_loc_tauAction_current, stated for an arbitrary triple and domain.
 - Step 6: "(M ∩ B_r, θ, ξ) satisfies the triple conditions, oriented by tangent locality". This is triple_inter_open = br_loc_triple_inter_open, stated for an arbitrary open V and target domain U′.
 Both are reusable whenever an integer multiplicity current is truncated to an open set. The polyhedral-approximation and flat-convergence branches use the same pattern.
(ii) Restriction theory: (H2) locally finite mass of T; existence and finite M_W-mass of R = T⌞A′ (step 3); the identification T⌞B_r = τ(M ∩ B_r) ((H4)(i),(ii),(iv), step 4); and the bound M_W((∂T)⌞B_r) ≤ M_W(∂T) ((H4)(iii), step 4). These are the three parts of the accepted iwl_restriction_theory:
 - (R0): a measure representation gives locally finite mass;
 - (R1): restrictions of a current to the same set are equal;
 - (R2): restrictions exist, and M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A) ≤ μ(W) = M_W(X).
 Reusing it gives the conclusions of the cut-off arguments (H3)–(H4) without re-proving them.
(iii) The remaining steps are accepted declarations:
 - step 7 (cut-off χ = 1 near B̄_r, locality of d, supremum) is exactly polyhedral_approx_boundary_mass_cutoff;
 - M(X) < ∞ (step 5) follows from the mass identity fiw_im_mass_formula;
 - the local agreement X = T near x₀ (step 5) is ltg_tau_congr_on_open;
 - the integrability in the representation (Hⁿ⌞M, θξ) (step 3) is ltg_tau_integrable;
 - (H0) is fiw_ims_tt_unit_bound, in the sharper operator-norm form;
 - tangent locality is br_weightedTangent_congr, which is the parent's own declared sibling dependency.
Splitting therefore leaves only two genuinely new obligations, each with a short independent proof. The parent becomes a bookkeeping assembly, already kernel-checked.

0. T is integer multiplicity: T = τ(M, θ, ξ) on Dⁿ(U) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ and θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M.
1. (Representation; supplied step 3.) Let μ₀ := H⌞M and v₀(x) := θ(x)ξ(x), so v₀(x)(ω(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)). For ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) (continuous, compactly supported, tsupport ω ⊆ U), tau_integrable (b) makes this μ₀-integrable, and T(ω) = tauAction = ∫ v₀(ω) dμ₀. Hence IsMeasureRepresentation T μ₀ v₀.

 - μ_T with IsMassMeasure T μ_T;
 - a restriction R of T to the Borel annulus A′ := {x ∈ U : r₀/2 < f(x) < r₀};

As M ⊆ U, A ∩ M = M ∩ B_r. So IsRestriction T A S₂ holds with the representation (μ₀, v₀), and restriction_theory (R1) gives A₁ = S₂.
12. (Local agreement; supplied step 5.) Let η ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ B_r. Apply tau_congr_on_open with (M, M ∩ B_r) and V = B_r; note (M Δ (M ∩ B_r)) ∩ B_r = ∅. It gives T(η) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(η) = τ(M ∩ B_r, θ, ξ)(η) = X(testFormOnInclusion η), since testFormOnInclusion keeps the underlying form.
13. (M(∂X) < ∞; supplied step 7.)
 (a) Apply boundary_mass_cutoff with U₁ = ℝ^P, U₂ = U, W, V = B_r, X and A₁. Here closure B_r = B̄_r is compact and B̄_r ⊆ W. Its hypothesis holds: if η = η′ on B_r, then X(η) = ∫_{M∩B_r} θξ(η) dH = ∫_{M∩B_r} θξ(η′) dH = S₂(η′) = A₁(η′) (setIntegral_congr_fun₀; M ∩ B_r is null-measurable). Hence M(∂X) ≤ M_W(∂A₁).
 (b) By step 7, ∂A₁(ψ) = S_r(ψ) + B₁(ψ). So for ψ admissible for M_W, ofReal ∂A₁(ψ) ≤ M_W(S_r) + M_W(B₁) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le, le_massOn).
 (c) Therefore M_W(∂A₁) ≤ M_W(S_r) + M_W(B₁) < ∞ by steps 6 and 8.
14. (Conclusion.) r > 0, B_r ⊆ U, and X ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity with M(X) < ∞, M(∂X) < ∞ and X(η) = T(η) for every η ∈ D^{m+1}(U) with tsupport η ⊆ B_r(x₀).

  intro hSlice P m U hU T hTIM hbd x₀ hx₀
  -- Step 0: the triple of `T`.
  obtain ⟨M, θ, ξ, hTr, hθN, hT⟩ := hTIM

      (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) hcont ω.property.1.2 ω.property.2

    · rw [hT ω]
      simp only [tauAction, ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
  have hRT := Submission.iwl_restriction_theory

    hRT.1 P (m + 1) U hU T _ _ hRep W hW
  -- Step 3: radii.

  have hXmass : X.mass < ∞ := by

      ext x

    rw [hset]
    simp only [ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]

    exact lt_of_le_of_lt hle (ENNReal.add_lt_top.mpr ⟨hSr, hB₁W⟩)
  have hXb : X.boundary.mass < ∞ := lt_of_le_of_lt hcut hbdA

subproblems.title: τ(M, θ, ξ) of a rectifiable triple is a current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V, M ⊆ ℝ^P (V arbitrary, not necessarily open), θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λₙ(ℝ^P) (n-vectors, NVector (Eucl P) n = continuous linear functionals on n-covectors). Assume (M, θ, ξ) satisfies the triple conditions of Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 relative to V (IsRectifiableTriple V n M θ ξ): M ⊆ V is Hⁿ-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable, θ > 0 on M, θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ V, ξ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable, and for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, ξ(x) = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ for an orthonormal τ spanning a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) (tauAction n M θ ξ ω) defines a current: there is X ∈ Dₙ(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V n: an ℝ-linear functional on the test forms Dⁿ(V) that is sequentially continuous in Simon's test-form topology) with X(ω) = τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(V).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple V n M θ ξ → ∃ X : GeometricCurrentOn V n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, X ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (H0) and (H2) of the parent proof ("T_A is linear and sequentially continuous, since test-form convergence implies uniform convergence", with the pointwise bound |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ c|α|), stated for an arbitrary rectifiable triple. In the parent it is applied with V = ℝ^P and the triple (M ∩ B_r(x₀), θ, ξ) supplied by the sibling triple_inter_open; this gives the current X = τ(M ∩ B_r(x₀), θ, ξ) of steps 5–6, and the domain restriction of X to U is the parent's T_{B_r} (step 4). Here the bound (H0) is used in the sharper operator-norm form of the sibling unit_bound, so no comparison constant c is needed.

Notation. H := Hⁿ = μHE[n]. For an n-covector α (a continuous alternating map), ‖α‖ is its operator norm. For ω ∈ Dⁿ(V) (a C^∞ n-form with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ V; TestFormOn V n) put F_ω(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) and τ(ω) := tauAction n M θ ξ ω = ∫_M F_ω dH. Openness of V is never used.

1. (Integrability.) Let ω ∈ Dⁿ(V). Then ω is continuous (being C^∞), has compact support, and tsupport ω ⊆ V. By the sibling tau_integrable (ltg_tau_integrable, second conjunct (b)), applied to IsRectifiableTriple V n M θ ξ and ω, the function F_ω is H-integrable on M.
2. (Pointwise bound.) By the orientation field of the triple, for H⌞M-a.e. x there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. For every such x the sibling unit_bound (fiw_ims_tt_unit_bound) gives |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every n-covector α. Moreover H⌞M-a.e. x lies in M (M is H-null-measurable, so ae_restrict_mem₀ applies), and θ(x) > 0 for every x ∈ M (field pos). Let G be the set of x ∈ M at which the bound of this step holds; H⌞M-a.e. x lies in G.
3. (Linearity.) Let ω, η ∈ Dⁿ(V) and c ∈ ℝ. The underlying forms satisfy (ω + η)(x) = ω(x) + η(x) and (cω)(x) = c·ω(x), and each ξ(x) is linear, so F_{ω+η}(x) = F_ω(x) + F_η(x) and F_{cω}(x) = c·F_ω(x) for every x. Since F_ω and F_η are integrable on M (step 1), τ(ω + η) = ∫_M (F_ω + F_η) dH = τ(ω) + τ(η) (additivity of the Bochner integral, integral_add), and τ(cω) = ∫_M c·F_ω dH = c·τ(ω) (integral_const_mul, which needs no integrability). Hence L(ω) := τ(ω) is an ℝ-linear map Dⁿ(V) → ℝ.
4. (Uniform smallness.) Let (ω_j) be a sequence in Dⁿ(V) converging to 0 in Simon's test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). By definition there is a compact K ⊆ V with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and for every k ∈ ℕ the k-th iterated derivatives of ω_j converge uniformly on K to those of the zero form. For k = 0 the iterated derivative has the same norm as the form itself, ‖D⁰ω_j(x)‖ = ‖ω_j(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), and D⁰0 = 0. Hence for every δ > 0 there is j₀ such that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < δ for all j ≥ j₀ and all x ∈ K.
5. (Majorant.) K is compact and K ⊆ V, so θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K (field integrableOn). K is closed, hence Borel; therefore 1_K·θ is H⌞M-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff together with (H⌞M)⌞K = H⌞(K ∩ M), Measure.restrict_restrict) and ∫_M 1_K θ dH = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH =: C (integral_indicator).
6. (Estimate.) Let ε > 0, put δ := ε/(|C| + 1) > 0, and let j ≥ j₀ with j₀ from step 4 for this δ. For every x ∈ G (step 2):
   - if x ∈ K: |F_{ω_j}(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ δ·θ(x) = δ·1_K(x)θ(x), using θ(x) > 0, step 2 and step 4;
   - if x ∉ K: x ∉ tsupport ω_j (as tsupport ω_j ⊆ K), so ω_j(x) = 0 and F_{ω_j}(x) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0 = δ·1_K(x)θ(x).
   Thus |F_{ω_j}| ≤ δ·1_Kθ holds H⌞M-a.e. The right side is H⌞M-integrable (step 5), so |L(ω_j)| = |∫_M F_{ω_j} dH| ≤ ∫_M δ·1_Kθ dH = δ·C ≤ δ·|C| < ε (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le; the last inequality is ε|C| < ε(|C| + 1)).
7. (Continuity.) Step 6 shows L(ω_j) → 0 for every sequence ω_j → 0 in Dⁿ(V). This is exactly the continuity field continuous' of GeometricCurrentOn V n.
8. (Conclusion.) X := ⟨L, step 7⟩ ∈ Dₙ(V), and X(ω) = L(ω) = tauAction n M θ ξ ω for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(V), by definition of L. ∎

Formalization notes. The current is built as ⟨{ toFun := fun ω => tauAction n M θ ξ ω, map_add', map_smul' }, continuous'⟩. Lemmas used: integral_add, integral_const_mul, integral_congr_ae, Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff, norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero, integrable_indicator_iff, integral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict, ae_restrict_mem₀, image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport, norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, Metric.tendsto_nhds. Appendix (formalization aid; kernel-checked Lean proof of exactly the frozen type, in the contract scope `namespace GMT.Ch06` with the contract's `open`s):

theorem Submission.br_loc_tauAction_current : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple V n M θ ξ → ∃ X : GeometricCurrentOn V n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, X ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω := by
  intro P n V M θ ξ hTr
  have hint : ∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, IntegrableOn
      (fun x => θ x * ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x)) M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) :=
    fun ω => (Submission.ltg_tau_integrable P n V M θ ξ hTr).2 _
      ω.property.1.1.continuous ω.property.1.2 ω.property.2
  have hub : ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M),
      ∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) n, |ξ x α| ≤ ‖α‖ := by
    filter_upwards [hTr.orients] with x hx
    obtain ⟨τ, hτ, -, hξ⟩ := hx
    exact Submission.fiw_ims_tt_unit_bound P n τ (ξ x) hτ hξ
  let L : CurrentOn V n :=
    { toFun := fun ω => tauAction n M θ ξ ω
      map_add' := by
        intro ω η
        simp only [tauAction]
        rw [← integral_add (hint ω) (hint η)]
        refine integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => ?_))
        simp only [Submodule.coe_add, Pi.add_apply, map_add, mul_add]
      map_smul' := by
        intro c ω
        simp only [tauAction, RingHom.id_apply, smul_eq_mul]
        rw [← integral_const_mul]
        refine integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun x => ?_))
        simp only [Submodule.coe_smul, Pi.smul_apply, map_smul, smul_eq_mul]
        ring }
  refine ⟨⟨L, ?_⟩, fun ω => rfl⟩
  intro ωs hconv
  obtain ⟨K, hK, hKV, hsupp, -, hderiv⟩ := hconv
  have hIK : IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) :=
    hTr.integrableOn K hK hKV
  set C : ℝ := ∫ x in M ∩ K, θ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) with hC
  have hgint : Integrable (K.indicator θ) ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) := by
    rw [integrable_indicator_iff hK.measurableSet, IntegrableOn,
      Measure.restrict_restrict hK.measurableSet, inter_comm]
    exact hIK
  have hgC : ∫ x, K.indicator θ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) = C := by
    rw [integral_indicator hK.measurableSet, Measure.restrict_restrict hK.measurableSet,
      inter_comm]
  -- uniform smallness of the forms on `K`
  have hsmall : ∀ δ > 0, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ∀ x ∈ K,
      ‖(ωs j : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x‖ < δ := by
    intro δ hδ
    have h0 := (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff.mp (hderiv 0)) δ hδ
    filter_upwards [h0] with j hj x hx
    have := hj x hx
    rw [dist_comm, dist_eq_norm] at this
    simpa [norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero] using this
  rw [Metric.tendsto_nhds]
  intro ε hε
  have hδ : 0 < ε / (|C| + 1) := by positivity
  filter_upwards [hsmall _ hδ] with j hj
  rw [Real.dist_eq, sub_zero]
  have hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M),
      ‖θ x * ξ x ((ωs j : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x)‖ ≤
        (ε / (|C| + 1)) * K.indicator θ x := by
    filter_upwards [hub, ae_restrict_mem₀ hTr.nullMeasurableSet] with x hx hxM
    have hθ := hTr.pos x hxM
    by_cases hxK : x ∈ K
    · rw [indicator_of_mem hxK, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul, abs_of_pos hθ]
      calc θ x * |ξ x ((ωs j : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x)|
          ≤ θ x * ‖(ωs j : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x‖ :=
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hx _) hθ.le
        _ ≤ θ x * (ε / (|C| + 1)) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hj x hxK).le hθ.le
        _ = ε / (|C| + 1) * θ x := mul_comm _ _
    · have hz : (ωs j : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = 0 :=
        image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport (fun h => hxK (hsupp j h))
      rw [indicator_of_notMem hxK, hz, map_zero, mul_zero, norm_zero, mul_zero]
  have hle := norm_integral_le_of_norm_le (hgint.const_mul (ε / (|C| + 1))) hbound
  rw [integral_const_mul, hgC, Real.norm_eq_abs] at hle
  change |∫ x in M, θ x * ξ x ((ωs j : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x)
    ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))| < ε
  calc _ ≤ ε / (|C| + 1) * C := hle
    _ ≤ ε / (|C| + 1) * |C| := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (le_abs_self C) hδ.le
    _ < ε := by
      rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_lt_iff₀ (by positivity)]
      nlinarith [abs_nonneg C]
proof_key_steps: For ω ∈ Dⁿ(V), x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is Hⁿ-integrable on M (sibling tau_integrable), so ω ↦ ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ is ℝ-linear.
By the orientation condition and the sibling unit_bound, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x and all α; θ > 0 on M.
If ω_j → 0 in Dⁿ(V), all supports lie in one compact K ⊆ V and sup_K ‖ω_j‖ → 0 (order-0 uniform convergence, ‖D⁰ω‖ = ‖ω‖).
Hence |τ(ω_j)| ≤ (sup_K ‖ω_j‖)·∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0, the integral being finite by the triple's local integrability on the compact K ⊆ V.
The linear, sequentially continuous functional τ(M, θ, ξ) is a current X ∈ Dₙ(V) with X(ω) = tauAction n M θ ξ ω.

subproblems.title: Restricting a rectifiable triple to an open set
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, U′, V, M ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λₙ(ℝ^P), and assume IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ (the triple conditions of Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 relative to U, with Hⁿ = μHE[n] and orientation by weighted approximate tangent spaces of (M, θ)). Suppose V is open, M ∩ V ⊆ U′, and θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ V ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U′. Then IsRectifiableTriple U′ n (M ∩ V) θ ξ: the restricted triple (M ∩ V, θ, ξ) satisfies all triple conditions relative to U′, including the orientation condition with respect to the weighted approximate tangent spaces of (M ∩ V, θ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U U' V M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → IsOpen V → M ∩ V ⊆ U' → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U' → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ V ∩ K) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → IsRectifiableTriple U' n (M ∩ V) θ ξ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof ("M_r ⊆ M is null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable; θ > 0; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M_r ≤ H⌞M; orientation: by the sibling tangent_locality with (M′, θ′) := (M ∩ B_r, θ), V := B_r, (M Δ (M ∩ B_r)) ∩ B_r = ∅"), for an arbitrary open V and target domain U′. The local integrability on U′ depends on U′ and is therefore a hypothesis; the parent discharges it for U′ = ℝ^P, V = B_r(x₀) from the integrability of θ on M ∩ B̄_r(x₀) (B̄_r(x₀) ⊆ U compact), since M ∩ B_r(x₀) ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ B̄_r(x₀).

Notation. H := Hⁿ = μHE[n]; H⌞A := H.restrict A. We verify the seven fields of IsRectifiableTriple U′ n (M ∩ V) θ ξ, using the fields of the given triple (M, θ, ξ).

1. (subset) M ∩ V ⊆ U′ is a hypothesis.
2. (nullMeasurableSet) M is H-null-measurable (given field) and V is open, hence Borel. The intersection of an H-null-measurable set with a measurable set is H-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.inter), so M ∩ V is H-null-measurable.
3. (countablyRectifiable) M is countably n-rectifiable: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with H(M₀) = 0 and each F_j Lipschitz. The same M₀ and F_j cover M ∩ V ⊆ M, so M ∩ V is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
4. (pos) If x ∈ M ∩ V then x ∈ M, so θ(x) > 0.
5. (integrableOn) For every compact K ⊆ U′, θ is H-integrable on (M ∩ V) ∩ K by hypothesis.
6. (aestronglyMeasurable) Since M ∩ V ⊆ M, H⌞(M ∩ V) ≤ H⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono). ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M (given field), hence for the smaller measure H⌞(M ∩ V) (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
7. (orients)
   (a) The orientation statement of (M, θ, ξ) holds for H⌞M-a.e. x; since M ∩ V ⊆ M it holds for H⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). By step 2, H⌞(M ∩ V)-a.e. x belongs to M ∩ V (ae_restrict_mem₀).
   (b) Fix x with both properties: x ∈ M ∩ V, and there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (span(range τ)) and ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ.
   (c) (M Δ (M ∩ V)) ∩ V = ∅: M Δ (M ∩ V) = (M ∖ (M ∩ V)) ∪ ((M ∩ V) ∖ M) = M ∖ V, which is disjoint from V. Hence H((M Δ (M ∩ V)) ∩ V) = H(∅) = 0.

Conventions (fixed for this proof). ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P. Hᵏ := μHE[k], the normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure (a positive constant multiple of μH[k]; it equals Lebesgue measure on a k-dimensional Euclidean space, and μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure). D_k(U) := GeometricCurrentOn U k; D^k(U) := TestFormOn U k (C^∞ k-forms on ℝ^P with compact tsupport contained in U). I(k,P) := the strictly increasing maps {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}; for I ∈ I(k,P), e_I := (e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(k)}) and dx^I is the constant k-covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} (J ∈ I(k,P)); every k-covector is α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (the norm used in the definition of mass), and ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a form ω. For a k-vector w (an element of NVector = the dual of the k-covectors) put w^I := w(dx^I) and |w|_* := (Σ_I (w^I)²)^{1/2}; then w(α) = Σ_I α(e_I) w^I, so |w(α)| ≤ |α| |w|_* (Cauchy–Schwarz). M_W(X) := X.massOn W, M(X) := X.mass = M_U(X), spt X := X.support, X_j ⇀ X := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary. τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) := tauAction = ∫_M θ ⟨ω,ξ⟩ dHᵏ with ⟨ω,ξ⟩(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)); "i.m." := IsIntegerMultiplicity; "X⌞A" denotes a current S with IsRestriction X A S; W ⊂⊂ U := CompactlyContainedOpen W U. Source: (P1) of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, 2.7–2.9 (representation of currents of locally finite mass by the Riesz Representation Theorem, Ch. 1, 4.14; the characterization 2.8 of μ_T; the restriction 2.9), together with the independence of the restriction from the chosen representation that the contract's IsRestriction (2.9) refers to ("the result does not depend on the representation (uniqueness of the vector measure T⃗ μ_T)").

Fact used. (F1) If tsupport ω ⊆ W then |X(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ M_W(X): if ‖ω‖ = 0 then ω = 0; otherwise ±ω/‖ω‖ is admissible in the definition of M_W(X).

Part (R0): a measure representation forces locally finite mass.
1. Let (μ,v) be a measure representation of X ∈ D_k(U) (IsMeasureRepresentation: for every ω ∈ D^k(U), x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and X(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ), and let W ⊂⊂ U. Choose φ ∈ C_c^∞(U) with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 and φ = 1 on the compact set closure(W) ⊆ U. For each I ∈ I(k,P), φ·dx^I ∈ D^k(U), so x ↦ φ(x) v^I(x) is μ-integrable and c_I := ∫_{closure W} |v^I| dμ < ∞.
2. If ω is admissible for M_W (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), then |v(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| |v(x)|_* ≤ Σ_I |v^I(x)| 1_{closure W}(x), so X(ω) ≤ Σ_I c_I. Hence M_W(X) ≤ Σ_I c_I < ∞.

Part (R1): restrictions are unique.
3. Let S_1, S_2 be restrictions of X to A, via representations (μ_1,v_1), (μ_2,v_2) of X (so A is measurable and S_l(ω) = ∫_A v_l(ω) dμ_l). As in step 1, ∫_K |v_l^I| dμ_l < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U and every I. Hence ν_l^I(B) := ∫_B v_l^I dμ_l (Borel B ⊆ U) defines signed Borel measures on U of locally finite total variation.
4. For φ ∈ C_c^∞(U): ∫ φ dν_1^I = X(φ dx^I) = ∫ φ dν_2^I. Every φ ∈ C_c(U) is the uniform limit of mollifications φ_ε ∈ C_c^∞(U) supported in a fixed compact subset K of U; by dominated convergence (|v_l^I| is μ_l-integrable on K) the identity extends to all φ ∈ C_c(U).
5. Hence ν_1^I = ν_2^I on Borel subsets of U: the positive locally finite Borel measures λ_1 := (ν_1^I)⁺ + (ν_2^I)⁻ and λ_2 := (ν_2^I)⁺ + (ν_1^I)⁻ on U (Jordan decompositions) have equal integrals against every φ ∈ C_c(U); locally finite Borel measures on the open set U ⊆ ℝ^P (a locally compact, σ-compact metric space) are regular and are determined by these integrals (Riesz uniqueness, Simon Ch. 1, 4.12; Mathlib `Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported`). So λ_1 = λ_2.
6. Let ω ∈ D^k(U); write ω = Σ_I ω_I dx^I with ω_I := ω(·)(e_I) ∈ C_c^∞(U), so v_l(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) v_l^I(x), and ω vanishes off the compact K := tsupport ω ⊆ U. Then S_l(ω) = Σ_I ∫_{A∩K} ω_I dν_l^I, which by step 5 is the same for l = 1, 2. Thus S_1(ω) = S_2(ω) for all ω, and S_1 = S_2 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).

Part (R2): mass measure, existence of restrictions, mass identity. Assume M_W(X) < ∞ for all W ⊂⊂ U. Let N := #I(k,P) and identify a k-covector α with its coefficient vector (α(e_I))_I ∈ ℝ^N; this is an isometry between |·| and the Euclidean norm of ℝ^N.
7. (Extension to continuous forms.) Let K_c(U;ℝ^N) be the continuous maps φ : U → ℝ^N with compact support in U. For such φ choose W ⊂⊂ U with spt φ ⊆ W; componentwise mollification gives test forms ω_ε with tsupport ω_ε ⊆ W for small ε, ‖ω_ε − φ‖ → 0 and |ω_ε| ≤ sup|φ| pointwise (mollification is an average and the Euclidean ball is convex). By (F1), |X(ω_ε) − X(ω_δ)| ≤ M_W(X)‖ω_ε − ω_δ‖ → 0, so L(φ) := lim_ε X(ω_ε) exists, does not depend on the approximating sequence, is linear, equals X on test forms, and |L(φ)| ≤ M_W(X) sup|φ| whenever spt φ ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U. Moreover, for every open W′ ⊆ U,
   sup{L(φ) : φ ∈ K_c(U;ℝ^N), spt φ ⊆ W′, |φ| ≤ 1} = M_{W′}(X):
   "≥" since admissible test forms are such φ; "≤" since for spt φ compact ⊆ W′ the mollifications are admissible for M_{W′} when ε is small, and L(φ) = lim X(ω_ε).
8. (Riesz.) L is a locally bounded linear functional on K_c(U;ℝ^N). By the Riesz Representation Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 4.14; SimonGMT `simon_theorem_4_14`, on the locally compact Hausdorff space U with the finite-dimensional Hilbert space ℝ^N) there are a Radon measure μ_0 on U and a μ_0-measurable ν : U → ℝ^N with |ν| = 1 μ_0-a.e. and L(φ) = ∫ ⟨φ, ν⟩ dμ_0; moreover μ_0 is the total variation measure of L: by (∗) in the proof of 4.14 (the envelope identity sup{L(φ) : |φ| ≤ g} = ∫ g dμ_0 for g ∈ C_c(U), g ≥ 0; SimonGMT `vectorFunctionalEnvelopeMeasure`) and inner regularity of μ_0 on open sets, μ_0(W′) = sup{L(φ) : spt φ ⊆ W′, |φ| ≤ 1} for every open W′ ⊆ U. By step 7, μ_0(W′) = M_{W′}(X) for every open W′ ⊆ U. Define the Borel measure μ on ℝ^P by μ(B) := μ_0(B ∩ U), and replace ν by a Borel function equal to it μ_0-a.e. Then μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0 and μ(W) = M_W(X) for every W ⊂⊂ U, i.e. IsMassMeasure X μ.
9. (Representation.) Let v(x) be the k-vector with coefficients v^I(x) := ν_I(x) for x ∈ U (v := 0 off U), i.e. v(x)(α) := Σ_I α(e_I) ν_I(x). For ω ∈ D^k(U): |v(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| |ν(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖ 1_{tsupport ω}(x) μ-a.e., which is μ-integrable since tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and μ is finite on it; and X(ω) = L(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ. So (μ, v) is a measure representation of X, with |v|_* = 1 μ-a.e.
10. (Existence of restrictions.) For a Borel set A ⊆ ℝ^P put S_A(ω) := ∫_A v(x)(ω(x)) dμ. S_A is linear on D^k(U); it is sequentially continuous: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology (tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for a fixed compact K ⊆ U and ω_j → 0 uniformly), then |S_A(ω_j)| ≤ ‖ω_j‖ μ(K) → 0. Thus S_A ∈ D_k(U) and IsRestriction X A S_A holds via the representation (μ, v).
11. (Mass identity.) Let S be any restriction of X to a set A (so A is measurable) and W ⊆ U open. By (R1), S = S_A.
   "≤": for admissible ω (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1), S_A(ω) ≤ ∫_{A∩W} |ω||v|_* dμ ≤ μ(W ∩ A).
   "≥": let K ⊆ A ∩ W be compact and ε > 0. By Lusin's theorem (μ_0 Radon, ν measurable) there is a compact K′ ⊆ K with μ(K ∖ K′) < ε such that ν|_{K′} is continuous and |ν| = 1 on K′; by outer regularity there is an open O with K′ ⊆ O, closure(O) compact ⊆ W, μ(O ∖ K′) < ε. Extend ν|_{K′} (Tietze, componentwise), compose with the radial retraction of ℝ^N onto its closed unit ball and multiply by a cutoff in C_c(O) equal to 1 on K′: this gives φ ∈ K_c(U;ℝ^N) with spt φ ⊆ O, |φ| ≤ 1, φ = ν on K′. Then ∫_A ⟨φ,ν⟩ dμ ≥ μ(K′) − μ(O ∖ K′) ≥ μ(K) − 2ε. The mollifications ω_ε of φ are admissible for M_W for small ε and converge to φ uniformly with supports in closure(O), so S_A(ω_ε) → ∫_A ⟨φ,ν⟩ dμ (dominated convergence). Hence M_W(S) ≥ μ(K) − 2ε. By inner regularity of the Radon measure μ_0 on the Borel set A ∩ W ⊆ U (valid also when μ(A ∩ W) = ∞, U being σ-compact), the supremum of μ(K) over compact K ⊆ A ∩ W is μ(W ∩ A). So M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A).
12. Steps 8, 10, 11 give (R2). Together with (R0) and (R1) this proves the three conjuncts. ∎

(R1): the coefficient signed measures of two representations agree on C_c^∞(U), hence on C_c(U), hence as measures (Riesz uniqueness), so the restrictions agree.
(R2): by the mass bound X extends to continuous compactly supported forms; the Riesz Representation Theorem (Ch. 1, 4.14) gives μ and ν with |ν| = 1 and μ(W′) = M_{W′}(X).

Mass identity M_W(S) = μ(W ∩ A): '≤' from |v|_* = 1, '≥' by Lusin approximation, mollification and inner regularity.

 (b) If ψ′(x) ≠ 0 then χ(x) ≠ 0, so support ψ′ ⊆ support χ. Hence tsupport ψ′ ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ C ⊆ W ⊆ U₂ by step 2, and ψ′ has compact support. Therefore ψ′ ∈ D^m(U₂) and tsupport ψ′ ⊆ W.
 (c) By step 3 and 2(a), |ψ′(x)| = |χ(x)|·|ψ(x)| ≤ 1·1 = 1 for all x.

The Fréchet derivative at x depends only on the germ at x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), so Dψ′(x) = Dψ(x). Therefore (dψ′)(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dψ′(x)) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dψ(x)) = (dψ)(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq). Thus the test forms dψ ∈ D^{m+1}(U₁) and dψ′ ∈ D^{m+1}(U₂) agree at every point of V.

6. (Comparison.) By step 5, hypothesis (H) applies with η := dψ and η′ := dψ′: ∂X(ψ) = X(dψ) = A(dψ′) = ∂A(ψ′). By step 4, ψ′ is admissible for M_W(∂A), so ofReal(∂A(ψ′)) ≤ M_W(∂A) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Hence ofReal(∂X(ψ)) ≤ M_W(∂A).

--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n for open W ⊆ U) and 2.7–2.8 (μ_T(W) = M_W(T)). The statement is used for real positive θ (rectifiable triples), as in the parent's preliminary (P1). The proof below is the standard duality argument.

Notation. H := μHE[n]. For α ∈ Λ^n(ℝ^P) and strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P put α_I := α(e_I), and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2}. This is a Euclidean norm on the finite-dimensional space Λ^n, since an alternating map vanishing on all e_I is 0. For a test form ω, ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)|. For each I let dx^I ∈ Λ^n be the covector with (dx^I)_J = δ_{IJ} (wedge of coordinate functionals), so α = Σ_I α_I dx^I.

1. (CB) (Cauchy–Binet bound; self-contained.) Let τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n) be orthonormal in ℝ^P and ζ := ±simpleNVector τ, so ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τ_n). Let A_{jk} := ⟨τ_j, e_k⟩ and, for strictly increasing I, let A_I be the n×n minor of A on the columns I.
   (a) For every α ∈ Λ^n, α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) det A_I. Expand τ_j = Σ_k A_{jk} e_k by multilinearity; terms with a repeated basis vector vanish by alternation; group the remaining terms by their increasing rearrangement I, the sign of the sorting permutation producing det A_I.
   (b) Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. Apply (a) to the alternating form α₀(v₁,…,v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} (the wedge of the functionals ⟨τ_i, ·⟩), for which α₀(e_I) = det A_I and α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1.
   Consequences: by Cauchy–Schwarz in the coordinates (α(e_I))_I, |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^n. The covector α^ζ := Σ_I ζ(dx^I) dx^I depends linearly on ζ and satisfies ζ(dx^I) = ±det A_I; hence |α^ζ| = 1 and ζ(α^ζ) = Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. For n = 0 these claims are immediate (ζ(α) = ±α(), |α| = |α()|). For n > P there is no orthonormal n-frame, so the orientation condition of IsRectifiableTriple forces H(M) = 0 and every statement below holds trivially.

2. (Inequality ≤.) Let ω be admissible for M_W(T), i.e. ω ∈ D^n(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. By the orientation condition of IsRectifiableTriple, for H-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ(x) with τ(x) orthonormal. So by step 1 (CB), |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1_W(x), since ω = 0 outside tsupport ω ⊆ W. The integrand θ ξ(ω) is integrable on M: it is bounded by θ·1_{M∩tsupport ω}, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U. Hence ofReal(T(ω)) = ofReal(∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH) ≤ ∫⁻_M ofReal(θ |ξ(ω)|) dH ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩W} ofReal θ dH. Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩W} ofReal θ dH.

3. (Inequality ≥: reduction to compact sets.) V := W ∩ U is open and M ∩ W = M ∩ V, since M ⊆ U. Let K_k := {x : |x| ≤ k, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/k} (or K_k := B̄_k(0) if V = ℝ^P; K_k := ∅ if V = ∅). These sets are compact, increasing, contained in V, and ⋃_k K_k = V. Since θ is a.e.-strongly measurable on each M ∩ K_k, monotone convergence gives ∫⁻_{M∩V} ofReal θ dH = sup_k ∫⁻_{M∩K_k} ofReal θ dH. So it suffices to show: for every compact K ⊆ V and every ε > 0 there is ω admissible for M_W(T) with T(ω) ≥ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH − ε. Note ∫_{M∩K} θ dH < ∞ by the integrability condition.

4. (A finite measure.) Fix K and ε. If K = ∅ the claim holds with ω := 0 (ofReal(T(0)) = 0 = ∫_{M∩∅} θ dH); assume K ≠ ∅. Choose δ₀ > 0 with K' := cthickening(δ₀, K) ⊆ V (possible since K is compact and V open); then K' is a compact subset of U. Let ν := θ H⌞(M ∩ K'), a finite Borel measure since θ is integrable on M ∩ K'. For 0 < δ ≤ δ₀ put V_δ := thickening(δ, K) ⊆ K'. The sets V_δ ∖ K decrease to ∅ as δ ↓ 0 (K is closed), so ν(V_δ ∖ K) → 0; fix δ ∈ (0, δ₀] with ν(V_δ ∖ K) < ε/4.

5. (Target field.) For H-a.e. x ∈ M put β(x) := α^{ξ(x)} (step 1, (CB)), so |β(x)| = 1 and ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1; put β := 0 elsewhere. β is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: it is a fixed linear function of ξ on the full-measure set where ξ(x) is a unit simple n-vector.

6. (Continuous approximation.) β·1_K is ν-integrable and |β 1_K| ≤ 1.
   - Density: compactly supported continuous functions are dense in L¹(ν; Λ^n), because ν is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P and hence regular (MeasureTheory.Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le). That lemma measures the error in Lean's operator norm on Λ^n, which is equivalent to |·| on this finite-dimensional space; the equivalence constant is absorbed into the tolerance. So there is γ₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P; Λ^n) with ∫ |γ₀ − β 1_K| dν < ε/4.
   - Truncation: let π(α) := α / max(1, |α|), the nearest-point retraction onto the closed unit ball of the Euclidean norm |·|; π is continuous, 1-Lipschitz and π(0) = 0. Let χ₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ χ₀ ≤ 1, χ₀ = 1 on K and tsupport χ₀ ⊆ V_δ. Put γ := χ₀ · (π ∘ γ₀).
   Then γ is continuous with compact tsupport ⊆ V_δ, and |γ| ≤ 1. Moreover |γ − β 1_K| ≤ |γ₀ − β 1_K| pointwise: on K, |π(γ₀) − π(β)| ≤ |γ₀ − β| because |β| ≤ 1; off K, |γ| ≤ |π(γ₀)| ≤ |γ₀|. Thus ∫ |γ − β 1_K| dν < ε/4.

7. (Smoothing.) Let ρ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫ ρ_σ = 1, support in B_σ(0)) and ω_σ := γ * ρ_σ, the convolution of the Λ^n-valued continuous function γ. Choose σ₀ > 0 with cthickening(σ₀, tsupport γ) ⊆ V_δ; this is possible since tsupport γ is compact and V_δ open, and also covers V_δ = ℝ^P. For 0 < σ < σ₀:
   - ω_σ is smooth, and tsupport ω_σ is compact and ⊆ V_δ;
   - |ω_σ(x)| ≤ ∫ ρ_σ(x − y) |γ(y)| dy ≤ 1, by convexity of the norm;
   - ω_σ → γ uniformly as σ → 0, by uniform continuity of γ.
   Fix such σ with sup |ω_σ − γ| · ν(ℝ^P) < ε/4 and let ω := ω_σ. Then ω ∈ D^n(U) (as V_δ ⊆ V ⊆ U), tsupport ω ⊆ V_δ ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ 1, so ω is admissible for M_W(T).

8. (Estimate.) Since ω = 0 off V_δ ⊆ K',
T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH = ∫ ξ(ω) dν = ∫_K ξ(β) dν + ∫_K ξ(ω − β) dν + ∫_{V_δ∖K} ξ(ω) dν.
   - The first term is ν(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH, because ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 for H-a.e. x ∈ M.
   - By step 1 (CB), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for H-a.e. x ∈ M. So the second term is ≥ −∫_K |ω − β| dν ≥ −∫ |ω − γ| dν − ∫ |γ − β 1_K| dν > −ε/4 − ε/4.
   - The third term is ≥ −ν(V_δ ∖ K) > −ε/4.
   Hence T(ω) > ∫_{M∩K} θ dH − ε, and M_W(T) ≥ ofReal(T(ω)) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).

9. (Conclusion.) By steps 3–8, M_W(T) ≥ ∫⁻_{M∩K} ofReal θ dH for every compact K ⊆ V, hence M_W(T) ≥ ∫⁻_{M∩W} ofReal θ dH. With step 2, T.massOn W = ∫⁻ x in M ∩ W, ofReal(θ x) ∂H. ∎

≤: every admissible ω gives T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n.
≥: exhaust W ∩ U by compacts K; approximate β·1_K (β = α^ξ) in L¹(θH^n⌞M) by continuous fields with |γ| ≤ 1 supported near K (radial retraction and cutoff).
Mollify (|ω| ≤ 1 is preserved by convexity) to get admissible ω with T(ω) ≥ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n − ε.

Notation. H := μHE[k]. For a k-covector α (a continuous alternating k-linear map), ‖α‖ is its operator norm, so |α(v₁,…,v_k)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_j |v_j|. The fields of IsRectifiableTriple used are nullMeasurableSet, integrableOn, aestronglyMeasurable and orients.

Hence x ↦ (ξ(x), ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞M, and so is its composition x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) with the evaluation map. The same holds for H⌞S whenever S ⊆ M, since H⌞S ≤ H⌞M. Taking ω constant equal to b gives the same for x ↦ ξ(x)(b).

 - By `integrableOn`, θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K.
 - Since M ∩ K ⊆ M, step 1 gives |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ ‖b‖ for H⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x.
 - By step 2, x ↦ ξ(x)(b) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞(M ∩ K).
 The product of an integrable function with an a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. bounded function is integrable. So x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(b) is H-integrable on M ∩ K.

 - θ is H-integrable on M ∩ K (`integrableOn`).
 - x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for H⌞(M ∩ K) (step 2), and |ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ C for H⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x (step 1).

subproblems.title: Locality of weighted approximate tangent spaces
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, M, M′ ⊆ ℝ^P, θ, θ′ : ℝ^P → ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P and V ⊆ ℝ^P open with x ∈ V. Then every linear subspace L ⊆ ℝ^P which is the weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.7 (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L: dim L = k and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHᵏ(y) → θ(x)∫_L f dHᵏ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x)) is also the weighted approximate tangent space of (M′, θ′) at x.

By definition, `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M θ x L` means: dim L = k (`finrank ℝ L = k`), and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P;ℝ), I_{M,θ}(r) := ∫_{η_r(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH(y) → θ(x)∫_L f dH as r ↓ 0 (limit along 𝓝[>]0).

1. (Null sets under blow-up.) If r > 0 and H(Z) = 0 then H(η_r(Z)) = 0. Indeed |η_r(a) − η_r(b)| = r⁻¹|a − b|, so η_r is Lipschitz with constant r⁻¹ and μH[k](η_r(Z)) ≤ r^{−k}μH[k](Z) (Mathlib `LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le`). Moreover H = c_k·μH[k] with c_k ∈ (0,∞) (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def`, `addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`), so H(Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](Z) = 0 ⇒ μH[k](η_r(Z)) = 0 ⇒ H(η_r(Z)) = 0.
2. (Elementary facts on η_r.) For r > 0, η_r is a bijection of ℝ^P with inverse y ↦ x + ry. Hence η_r(A ∩ B) = η_r(A) ∩ η_r(B), η_r(A ∖ B) = η_r(A) ∖ η_r(B) for all A, B, and η_r(V) = {y : x + ry ∈ V} is open (preimage of the open V under a continuous map).

Choose R > 0 with f(y) = 0 whenever |y| ≥ R (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded), and δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ V (V open, x ∈ V). We prove I_{M,θ}(r) = I_{M′,θ′}(r) for every r ∈ (0, δ/R). 6. (Step C: replacing θ by θ′.) ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_θ dH = ∫_{η_r(M∩V)} F_{θ′} dH. By hypothesis (H⌞(M∩V)){z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} = 0, so there is a Borel set N ⊇ {z : θ(z) ≠ θ′(z)} with (H⌞(M∩V))(N) = H(N ∩ (M∩V)) = 0 (`exists_measurable_superset_of_null`, `Measure.restrict_apply`). Let N′ := {y : x + ry ∈ N}, a Borel set. Then {y : F_θ(y) ≠ F_{θ′}(y)} ⊆ N′, and N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V) ⊆ η_r(N ∩ (M∩V)) (if y = η_r(z) with z ∈ M ∩ V and x + ry = z ∈ N). By step 1 the right side is H-null, so (H⌞η_r(M∩V))(N′) = H(N′ ∩ η_r(M∩V)) = 0; thus F_θ = F_{θ′} (H⌞η_r(M∩V))-a.e. and the integrals agree (`integral_congr_ae`).
7. (Step B: replacing M by M′.) η_r(M∩V) and η_r(M′∩V) are H-a.e. equal sets: by step 2 their differences are η_r((M∩V)∖(M′∩V)) and η_r((M′∩V)∖(M∩V)), both contained in η_r((M Δ M′) ∩ V), which is H-null by the hypothesis H((M Δ M′) ∩ V) = 0 and step 1. Hence H⌞η_r(M∩V) = H⌞η_r(M′∩V) (`ae_eq_set`, `Measure.restrict_congr_set`).
